findings.text: VCHIQ match entry holds a single fixed size name field of thirty two characters for device identification, with no additional match keys or driver data in this fragment.
VIO match entry holds two fixed size character arrays of thirty two bytes each, one for type and one for compatibility string, used as bus matching keys.
Virtio match entry holds two unsigned thirty two bit fields for device and vendor identifiers, enabling exact or wildcard matching.
Virtio wildcard identifier equals thirty two bits all set, namely hexadecimal FFFFFFFF, applicable to device matching.
WMI module alias prefix is the four character sequence w m i plus colon, used to form module aliases.
WMI match entry holds a constant GUID text field sized one more than UUID string length plus an opaque context pointer for driver use.

x86 CPU matching provides wildcard and range sentinels with vendor any as hexadecimal FFFF, family model stepping platform feature and type any as zero, stepping minimum zero and stepping maximum as hexadecimal F covering a full nibble.

x86 CPU match entry holds vendor family model steppings feature flags plus platform mask type and driver data, where feature denotes a bit index and flags are kernel internal and not for userspace export, with an alias name for the table entry type.
Zorro wildcard equals thirty two bits all set and modalias format is a fixed pattern starting with zorro colon i followed by eight uppercase hex digits.

Zorro match entry holds a thirty two bit identifier that may be the wildcard plus a union offering either an unsigned long driver data value or a constant pointer for driver private use, but not both at once.
Subsystem interface descriptor carries a name and a bus reference plus a list node and two callbacks for device arrival and departure, allowing a subsystem to observe devices.
Device type descriptor carries a name, attribute group table, uevent and devnode and release callbacks, and a power operations pointer, defining per type behavior.
Device sysfs attribute pairs a generic attribute with show and store handlers in both mutable and constant forms, selected to support read and write access with alternative signatures.
Extended device attribute augments a normal device attribute with an opaque variable pointer so generic show and store routines can operate on external storage.

Attribute construction chooses between mutable and constant handler slots based on handler type, with one build offering separate slots and another build collapsing to shared slots via pointer conversion.

Base attribute constructors create a named attribute with verified octal permissions and bound show and store handlers, with read only write only and read write shorthands using conventional permission sets.

Administrative and explicitly named attribute constructors vary only permission bits or exposed name while reusing the same handler binding, plus a lockdep ignoring variant that marks the attribute to bypass lock validation in one build and aliases the normal form otherwise.

Typed unsigned long integer boolean and read only string helpers build extended attributes that bind generic numeric or string show and store routines to a caller supplied variable, with the string form stripping write permission bits.
Default attribute permission facts are public read only octal 0444, public read write octal 0644, write only octal 0200, admin read only octal 0400 and admin read write octal 0600.
DMA parameter block carries maximum segment size, minimum alignment mask and segment boundary mask so low level drivers can convey scatter gather limits to IOMMU logic.
Device link progresses from none through dormant and available into consumer probe and active, ending in supplier unbind, with none encoded as negative one and dormant as zero.

Device link flag bits zero through nine denote stateless, autoremove consumer, runtime PM, RPM active, autoremove supplier, autoprobe consumer, managed, sync state only, inferred and cycle respectively.
Per device link tracking moves from no driver through probing to driver bound and finally unbinding, encoding the four phases as zero through three in order.
Removability enumeration orders not supported as zero, then unknown, fixed and removable, with zero reserved to mean the capability query is unsupported.
Link bookkeeping holds supplier and consumer lists plus a deferred sync list and a status value recording the current driver binding phase.
MSI info optionally holds an interrupt domain pointer and MSI device data pointer when generic MSI support is enabled, otherwise it is empty.

Physical location combines a panel choice among top bottom left right front back and unknown, a vertical choice among upper center lower, a horizontal choice among left center right, and two booleans for dock and lid association.

Device flag indices zero through nine denote ready to probe, can match, DMA IOMMU, DMA skip sync, DMA ops bypass, state synced, DMA coherent, of node reused, offline disabled and offline, with a count sentinel marking the total.

Central device object anchors identity via kobject plus parent private init name type bus driver and class references, separates platform and driver private pointers, carries driver override name under its own spinlock and a mutex for driver calls, tracks links power domain MSI DMA IOMMU NUMA firmware and device tree associations, DMA constraints pools and optional coherent and CMA and TLB areas, instance identifiers and sysfs groups, release callback, physical location, removability and a flag bitmap with generated test set clear assign and test and set accessors.

Device link object records supplier and consumer pointers with respective list nodes, an embedded link device, link status and flags, runtime PM reference and general reference counts plus removal work and a supplier preactivation marker owned by consumer probe, with a helper recovering the enclosing device from its kobject.

Driver invocation is serialized by the per device mutex via lock interruptible lock trylock and unlock helpers plus guard helpers, while driver override name is protected by its own spinlock and device resource list and DMA TLB pool list have dedicated spinlocks.

Driver override helpers set the override string with its length, test presence under lock, and match against a driver name returning nonzero on equality, zero on inequality and negative one when no override is set.

Simple device queries report IOMMU attachment by testing the IOMMU group pointer, report bus or class name with empty string fallback, get or set the MSI domain with null or no operation when MSI support is off, and set or ignore NUMA node depending on build.

Power and core state accessors expose subsystem data with null safe handling, uevent suppression level, sysfs registration state, async suspend enable disable and query gated on preparation, no PM marking, syscore marking, driver flags set and test, and smart suspend query defaulting false without sleep support.

Strict midlayer marking and query respect sleep build availability, sync state installer accepts null device or driverless device as success, rejects conflicting callbacks as busy and installs on first use, while removability setters and testers distinguish fixed versus removable and valid versus unsupported.

Child lookup helpers find by name or return any child via generic child iteration with name and match any predicates, offline support requires both bus offline and online callbacks, and lock class helper assigns a custom lockdep class to the device mutex.

Length macro selects compile time builtin evaluation when the argument is a constant expression and fortified runtime evaluation otherwise, so behavior differs between constant and non constant inputs.

Attribute handler duality risks mismatched const expectations across builds, and the lockdep ignoring form silently disables validation, so callers must ensure handler signatures and locking assumptions match the active build.
